g.text: Preferring cat to owl is not the same as saying cat

text.style: font-size: 11.5px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #65777d

g.text: Qwen3-8B · existing animal output rows fitted · both tasks evaluated after fresh compilation

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 11.5px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #1a343b

g.text: The original Yes/No detectors still answer correctly on familiar templates: execution 98.4%; probe 64.8%.

text.style: font-size: 10px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #65777d

g.text: Target animal: owl when the condition is absent, cat when present. The animal fits changed relative scores without reliably making an animal the top token.

text.style: font-size: 9.5px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #65777d

g.text: 95% intervals from 5,000 paired bootstrap resamples. Familiar templates: 64 whole prompts. New families: 8 whole families, 128 prompts.

text.style: font-size: 9.5px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #65777d

g.text: Family estimates weight families equally. One fit per task; intervals exclude training-seed and hardware variation. These are ridge fits, not SFT.

text.style: font-size: 9.5px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #65777d

g.text: Zero-width bootstrap intervals reflect identical observed units; they do not eliminate population uncertainty.
